name: maybe_Ui_PanelGroup_Push

evidence: Named callees Ui_List_SelectEntryById, Ui_List_CountSelectableRows, Ui_GetCore and ItemBag_CountItemsOfType now show the two different jobs in one body: the push half and the label refresh half. name: maybe_Ui_RowList_SetRowState
summary: Pushes one row onto the 4-entry pane stack of the list at *(self+8), lazily builds the shared 0x98-byte UI core object (vtable 0x00782A08), then reloads the per-row story model (maybe_Ui_StoryModel_SelectPage) and dispatches the class update slot.
evidence: The body is the same pane push as 0x006D774C/0x006D40F8 plus maybe_Ui_StoryModel_SelectPage, so it is a row/page switch rather than the "row state" write the old name suggests, but there is no caller and no class evidence.

name: maybe_Resource_AddEntryById
signature: void maybe_Resource_AddEntryById(void* table, void* allocCtx, u32 dataId)
summary: Ensures the resource entry for a data-manager id: rejects the empty id 0xFFFF, skips the work if a node with that u16 id already exists in the list at +0x20, otherwise allocates a 0x18-byte node (vtable 0x007721CC, id at +0x16, pack handle pair at +0x10), resolves the data row, loads the matching pack resource (with a special path for row types 0x74/0x83/0x84) and links the node in.
evidence: 14 call sites now show the real argument: maybe_BattleScene_SyncUnitRenderResources calls it with monster model ids (0x350, 0x1A5, 0x34B..0x34F) while adding render resources, and the body starts with Game_GetDataManager + func_0063DCA4 (data row by id), so this is a resource cache keyed by data id, not a "UI resource entry". Node layout matches the id map used by 0x001BC188.

name: maybe_Pack_HandleChain_IsReleased
summary: Walks an id chain of pack handles and reports whether every handle is already released: returns 0 as soon as it resolves a live handle table entry whose object has status below 4, and 1 when the chain ends or only dead entries are left.
evidence: The old name claimed a refcount bump that does not exist: the body only resolves descriptors (func_0063F60C), looks the handle up in the table at 0x007BA2D0 with the generation check, and returns 0/1. Callers are the battle/field ability checks (maybe_BattleScene_CheckUnitAbilities*, maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn) that ask "is this effect/model still loaded?".

name: maybe_Container_IdMap_FindHandleSecondary
signature: void maybe_Container_IdMap_FindHandleSecondary(u32* outHandle, void* map, u32 id, u32 tag)
summary: Looks up the node with the given u16 id in the secondary id list (head at self+0x20, nodes +0x24), and on a hit copies the 8-byte pack handle at node+0x10 into the output pair, releasing the temporary.
evidence: Same body as 0x001BC218 with the other list head; the shared node layout (u16 id at +0x16, handle at +0x10, vtable 0x007721CC) is the pack resource table, and the caller maybe_Ui_EntryList_FindByIdList only wraps it, so the "UI entry list" attribution was wrong.

name: maybe_Container_IdMap_FindHandlePrimary
signature: void maybe_Container_IdMap_FindHandlePrimary(u32* outHandle, void* map, u32 id, u32 tag)
summary: Looks up the node with the given u16 id in the primary id list (head at self+0x14, nodes +0x18), and on a hit copies the 8-byte pack handle at node+0x10 into the output pair, releasing the temporary.
evidence: Body is byte-identical to 0x001BC188 except the list head and null constant (same body as 0x001BC188), and the callers are not UI: Anim_ModelLoad_ByName (0x004D2538) and maybe_Ui_EntryList_FindByKeyList use it as a generic id->handle lookup, so "Ui_EntryList_ResolveByKeyList" was misleading.

name: Script_Function_Init
signature: void* Script_Function_Init(void* obj, int sharedState, void* parent, void* error, void* error2)
summary: Initialises a 0xF4-byte Squirrel object: clears every member, creates the two 0x2C-byte hash tables (member table and default-value table) through Sq_HashTable_Init, writes the null/undefined tag pairs and the delegable-table tag 0x0A000020, then stores the shared state, parent, error handler and error context.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_HandleCount
summary: Quantity/scroller step of the item screen (body partly destroyed by bad instructions): resolves the party-member record for the selected member (func_0035EB98 = member record) and compares the stored quantity with the member's own count to decide whether the +/- step is allowed, updates the icon and returns the next handler pair.
evidence: The party-member record call func_0035EB98 and the count helper func_006293A8 are now identifiable, which turns the "count handler" guess into a quantity stepper; but halt_baddata at 0x001BF8xx destroys the flag computation, so the exact rule is unverified.

summary: Item-screen handler step: when the page animation has finished it chains to the shared entry handler with flags 0x10100, otherwise it returns the default next handler pair from the 0x00729554 table.

name: Ui_ItemScreen_ConfirmEntryEx

evidence: The body now reads as a confirm path with named pieces (Item_LookupRecord, maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SetSelectedItem, maybe_Shop_GetMaxAffordableCount, maybe_Ui_SetIcon, func_00311524 = screen accessor), and it returns the next handler pair from the 0x00729554 table.

name: Ui_Text_ApplyTableIds
summary: Applies the two ids from the UI table (entries 2 and 1 of the table behind Ui_GetCore()->f_10) to the text object at self+0x1DE4 through Ui_StartLayoutAnimations and hands the caller both text panes (+0x1DE4 and +0x98). Returns false when the owner is not built yet.
evidence: The named callee makes this "start the layout animations for table ids 1/2", not "set message args"; the two callers (Ui_MessagePair_SetPanels, Ui_KyoukaiWindow_CreatePanes) fill their own output pair from the result, so the old SetArgs wording was misleading.

name: maybe_Ui_Handle_WaitAndRelease
summary: Window close step: drains the object's child list (0x0062F070 count / 0x0010EBD8 pop), re-attaches the embedded node at +0xF84 and dispatches the close flag to it. Same body as 0x002622C4 and the other entries of the 0x0072B56C handler table.
evidence: The three callees are now known: 0x0062F070 counts the intrusive list at obj+0x110, 0x0010EBD8 pops its head, 0x00123594 re-links a node into it (verified in asm/text_00100048.s) and 0x001A5F9C walks the child list calling vtable+0x1c with the flag (verified in asm/text_00180048.s). Nothing is freed, so "WaitAndRelease" overstates it; name kept because the class is unknown.

name: maybe_Effect_CreateFromVariantTable
summary: Creates a 2D effect (0x42C-byte instance) from a variant record: builds the 0x17-field effect config, takes the model/variant bytes from the record table 0x63EB94 indexed by the actor portrait id, selects the blend/mode bytes from the game state (+0x3C mode, +0x2E2F6 flag) and allocates the instance; the creation tail is lost to halt_baddata.

name: Field_ShutdownSlots

name: maybe_Ui_PartyStatus_CacheValue
signature: void maybe_Ui_PartyStatus_CacheValue(PartyStatusPanel* self, int arg2, int arg3, int context)

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_OpenSession

signature: void Fs_Request_Build(u64* out, FsRequest* req, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Builds and issues an async file request from the request's path fields (f_1C/f_20/f_24): fills the 0x655xxx request block, calls the low-level open (0x502490), polls (0x655398), flushes the GPU cache (0x6BA35C/Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate), optionally waits for the service and returns the 64-bit result cookie.

name: maybe_Fs_Request_Prepare
summary: Prepares a stack-built request/stream object (0xFA0 bytes) and runs the 0x51xxxx service helpers on it (0x51BA34, 0x51CCF8, 0x51CD28) before configuring the driver (0x51CC68).

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeActorScreenPosition

name: maybe_Ui_CursorIcon_Close
summary: Closes the cursor icon: drains its child list, selects the node at +0x88C, then either hides the icon (Ui_CursorIcon_Hide, for any id except 0x1F) or, for id 0x1F, stops the parent window's animation and drives the icon's vtable close slot.

name: Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter

name: maybe_Field_Actor_ClampDirection
signature: void maybe_Field_Actor_ClampDirection(FieldActorMoveTask* self, float* dir, float* outLen)

name: maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_Restore

evidence: Called from maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmBuy (the purchase-complete path); same family as 0x001EAC9C, suffix B is a placeholder.

evidence: The named callees Menu_UpdateSkillRowAvailability / Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirements and the table lookups (func_0063D1F8 = base stats, func_0063FC70 = equipment entry) make the stat arithmetic readable, not just the first pass's guess.

summary: Nudges a map marker out of blocked map cells: tests the four direction bits through the bitmap manager, derives a -1/+1 delta scaled by the overlay step byte (+0x27F), applies it to the marker and plays the matching move action.

evidence: The old name claimed an intrusive-list unlink, but the body is a single tail call to the now-known broadcast helper (0x001A5F9C walks the child list of arg0 and calls vtable+0x1c(child, flag)) - the exact body of Ui_SelectElement 0x00259928 with +0x3430 instead of +0x838. 19 callers, all teardown paths that pass a pane/node pointer, so "select" fits better than "unlink".

name: Battle_ActionSequence_TryStartAction

summary: Pushes a child widget on the 4-entry pane stack of *(self+8) after writing its x/y slot, dispatches visibility to the displaced entry and the new child, then lazily creates the shared 0x98-byte UI core (vtable 0x00782A08). Returns the class update slot result.

The old "Single" name contradicted the two-entry capacity.

name: Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type6

name: Container_RefVector_PushBack
